key_insight: Eliminating stalled or redundant operators in ADAPT-VQE, especially when paired with correlated downfolding, makes the optimization faster, shallower, and more accurate within a fixed active space.
engineering_relevance: The approach lowers quantum circuit depth and iteration cost while improving energy estimates, making ADAPT-VQE more practical for near-term quantum chemistry workflows.
method: Detect non-contributing operators during ADAPT-VQE and remove them from the pool to avoid optimization stalls.
Compare two elimination strategies: with pool restoration and without pool restoration.
Combine ADAPT-VQE with OBDF downfolding to replace the bare active-space Hamiltonian with a correlated effective Hamiltonian that captures خارج-active-space dynamical correlation.
evidence_signal: Benchmarked in OpenFermion on linear H6 chain, H6 lattice, H6 ring, and N2, where operator elimination reduced circuit depth and iteration count, and OBDF-ADAPT-VQE produced energies closer to FCI than standard ADAPT-VQE in the same active space.
watch_item: Operator elimination and downfolded Hamiltonians may depend on detection thresholds, restoration policy, and active-space choice, so performance gains may not transfer uniformly across all molecules or noise settings.
paper_title: Reducing quantum resources for ADAPT-VQE via plateau-operator elimination and correlated mean-field downfolding
